name: Torres del Paine
tagline: Granite towers, turquoise lakes and glaciers in one of the world's great national parks.
highlight: Hiking to the base of the three granite towers at sunrise, when they glow red.
shortDescription: A UNESCO Biosphere Reserve in southern Patagonia, famous for the W Trek, the O Circuit, Grey Glacier, guanacos and pumas.
metaDescription: A Torres del Paine guide: the W Trek and O Circuit, Base Torres sunrise, Grey Glacier, wildlife, refugios and camping, getting there from Puerto Natales, costs and a four-day plan.

intro: Torres del Paine National Park is the crown jewel of Chilean Patagonia. Its landscape combines the sheer granite spires of the Paine massif, the striped Cuernos, glacial lakes in impossible shades of blue, and the huge Grey Glacier, set in a windswept steppe of guanacos and condors. It is a UNESCO Biosphere Reserve.

Most visitors come to hike. The W Trek takes four to five days, linking the Grey Glacier, the French Valley and the Base Torres viewpoint, while the O Circuit adds the remote back side of the massif in seven to ten days. Those short of time can do day hikes, boat trips and drives, and wildlife viewing is excellent, with guanacos, foxes, condors and, with luck, pumas.

The weather is notoriously changeable, and strong winds are common. Refugios and campsites must be reserved well in advance for the summer season, usually many months ahead. Puerto Natales is the base town, with gear shops, restaurants and tour operators.
